subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry/cloud) \u2014 Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry/cloud) — Acme Health

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and (proposed) next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Info classification & PII: Acme will send examples of the payloads/fields you consider PII. We discussed using a combination of in-product redaction + configurable retention windows for sensitive data.

2) Retention & logging controls: Redwood supports per-customer retention policies and request-level logging. For Hosted API customers we retain request/response logs for a default of 30 days (configurable). For Dedicated/Private we can commit to customer-controlled retention and longer-term archival options.

3) Data residency: You asked whether telemetry/logs and model I/O can be constrained to a region — yes, for Dedicated/Private we can ensure residency (US/EU). For Hosted, default is US (us-east-1) but we have EU-hosted options planned/available via marketplace/private deployments — see links below.

4) Third-party sharing / subprocessors: Telemetry and metrics are sent to our telemetry pipeline; we work with a small set of telemetry vendors and cloud providers. I've attached our current subprocessor matrix and SOC2 summary. The matrix lists vendors and the purpose of processing.

Next steps:
- I will attach the subprocessor matrix and SOC2 summary (attached).
- Please confirm which of the example payloads you consider PII and whether you require EU residency for logs/model data.
- If acceptable, propose a quick 30-min security/deep-dive with Vivek to go over the DPA/subprocessor details.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-matrix.csv, SOC2-summary.pdf, telemetry-integration-one-pager.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry/cloud) — Acme Health

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs inline: 

- Telemetry vendors: can you confirm the vendor names and whether any telemetry contains user-level identifiers (e.g., name, email, MRN)? We prefer telemetry to be strictly anonymous/pseudonymized.

- Residency: Acme requires logs and any PII-derived artifacts to remain in the US (for now). For our longer-term roadmap we may ask for EU residency; can you confirm how Hosted vs Dedicated differ on enforcement and contractual guarantees?

- Procurement: I copied procure@acmehealth.com — our procurement team will need the DPA + current subprocessor list for vendor review. Please include a single-file subprocessor export if possible.

Available for the 30-min security call tomorrow afternoon between 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Alicia Torres
Director, Product Security
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry/cloud) — Acme Health

Hi Alicia —

Answers inline: 

- Telemetry vendors: current telemetry providers are TelemetryOps (integrations@telemetryops.com) and LogStream (logstream@logstream.io). Telemetry we send to those vendors is metric/observability data (latency, error rates, aggregated usage). We do not intentionally send direct identifiers (name/email/MRN) to telemetry vendors for Hosted deployments — any identifiers are hashed/pseudonymized. 

- Residency: Hosted (default) stores logs in US regions (us-east-1). We can enable EU residency via a Dedicated deployment or our Private offering; for Dedicated we can contractually restrict log storage and backup locations to the EU/US endpoints. For Hosted we offer marketplace/private region options (AWS Marketplace flow) — however, contractual residency guarantees are available only for Dedicated/Private.

- Subprocessors export: attached (redwood-subprocessors-matrix.csv). Also attached SOC2 summary and a one-pager on telemetry integrations.

Vivek — can you run quick validation on the matrix for any flagged vendors we should surface to customer procurement? Also, recommend we prepare a short DPA excerpt that covers subprocessor notification timing and the option for Acme to request evidence (SOC2, penetration test summaries).

If tomorrow 2–4pm PT works, I can set the 30-min slot and include Vivek and Rishi.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (telemetry/cloud) — Acme Health

Thanks for the ping — quick internal notes: 

- I'll validate TelemetryOps & LogStream against our approved vendor list and call out any gaps.
- We should prepare a minimal data flow diagram (request/response, telemetry pipeline, storage locations) and a one-page DPA excerpt covering subprocessors and notification timing.
- For Hosted customers we need to be explicit: telemetry is anonymized but cannot be contractually restricted to a region without Dedicated/Private. Let's be clear in the DPA language to avoid procurement pushback.

Marissa — I'll attach the vendor-checklist and a draft DPA excerpt by EOD. Rishi, flag any legal/regulatory items.

-Vivek

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@acmehealth.com>
